title: How to Convert Hourly Rate to Annual Salary and Understand the Salary Cap
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual salary using the 38-hour week formula. Understand the salary cap for super, tax brackets, and Medicare levy.
salarySummary: For a standard 38-hour week, your annual salary is your hourly rate multiplied by 1,976 hours (38 × 52).

faqs.q: What is the casual loading and how does it affect my annual salary?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate, as set by the Fair Work Commission. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour becomes $33.05 per hour for casual employees. When converting to annual salary, multiply the casual rate by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks. The casual loading is paid instead of entitlements like annual leave and sick leave.

faqs.q: How does the super guarantee cap affect my annual pay?
faqs.a: The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. However, there is a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). If your annual salary exceeds this cap, your employer only pays super on the first $270,830. This is often called the 'salary cap' for super. For most workers, the cap does not apply if your salary is below that amount.

faqs.q: What are the tax brackets and Medicare levy for 2026–27 for residents?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are: nil on the first $18,200, then 15% up to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The tax-free threshold reduces the tax but not the Medicare levy. Your annual salary estimate uses these rates, but does not include HELP or surcharges.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert Hourly Rate to Annual Salary

To convert your hourly rate to an annual salary, use the simple formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. Most full-time roles are based on a 38-hour week, as set by the Fair Work Commission. If you work different hours, adjust the formula accordingly. For example, a 40-hour week would use 40 × 52.

### The 38-Hour Week Assumption

When we talk about annual salary on this site, we assume a standard 38-hour week unless stated otherwise. This is the ordinary hours for a full-time employee under the National Employment Standards. For part-time or casual roles, your hours may vary. The formula remains the same: multiply your hourly rate by your actual weekly hours and 52 weeks. If you are paid a salary, you can reverse the calculation to find your equivalent hourly rate.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly pay is simply weekly pay × 2. For a 38-hour week, that’s hourly × 76 hours. This is a common pay period for award-covered employees. Check your pay slip to confirm.

## National Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the base rate for award/agreement-free employees. Most workers are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) with minimum rates for each award.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate. For the minimum wage, that’s $33.05 per hour. When calculating your annual salary, include the casual loading if applicable. Do not add it again if your rate already includes it. Our [timesheet](/about) has a checkbox to add 25% casual loading automatically.

## Super Guarantee and the Salary Cap

Super is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% of your ordinary earnings. It is not deducted from your salary; it is an extra payment from your employer. However, there is a **salary cap** known as the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). If your annual salary exceeds this cap, your employer only pays super on the first $270,830. This is often called the 'salary cap' for super. For most workers, the cap does not apply if your salary is below that amount. Use our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page to estimate your super contributions.

## Tax and Medicare Levy

Your annual gross salary is taxed according to the 2026–27 resident tax rates: nil on the first $18,200, then 15% up to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. This estimate uses the full tax-free threshold and the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds for Medicare, as the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed. For a more accurate calculation, use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool.

## Example Calculation

Suppose you earn $30 per hour, casual, with 25% loading. Your casual rate is $37.50 per hour. For a 38-hour week, your weekly pay is $1,425. Annual gross is $1,425 × 52 = $74,100. Super at 12% on top is $8,892, but only up to the cap. Tax on $74,100 is approximately $14,092 (using the brackets). Medicare levy is $1,482. Your take-home pay is around $58,526 per year. This is an estimate; your actual pay may differ due to allowances, overtime, or salary sacrifice.

## Using the Timesheet

Our [timesheet](/) is the home page. Enter your base hourly rate. If you are casual, check the box to add 25% loading. The timesheet will calculate your weekly, fortnightly, and annual figures, including super and tax estimates. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Always verify with your employer or the Fair Work Ombudsman.

## Award and Agreement Free Employees

If you are not covered by an award or agreement, you are entitled to the National Minimum Wage. The Fair Work Commission sets special minimum wages for juniors, apprentices, and employees with disability. Use the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for details.

## Average Weekly Earnings

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports average weekly earnings for full-time adult ordinary time at $2,083.70 (May 2026). This is higher than the minimum wage and reflects typical award rates. Use the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page to compare.

## Final Notes

This article provides a general guide. Your actual pay depends on your award, agreement, or contract. Always refer to official sources like the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Australian Taxation Office. The salary cap for super is an important limit to understand if your earnings are high. For more details, see the [reference tables](/data).
